text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A cabinet meeting under President Saddam Hussein reviews obstacles put by the United States on the way of implementing the memorandum of understanding -- oil-for-food deal.
- Two ships loaded with sugar are expected to arrive soon at Umm Qasr port in southern Iraq.
- Iraq's justice minister holds news conference in Ankara.
- National Assembly speaker says Iraq is keen to preserve Arab solidarity.
- Trade ministry announces further reductions in food prices.
- Ship loaded with rice arrives at Umm Qasr port.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- Iraq and Italy discuss ways to resume bilateral ties.
- Harvest of wheat and barley starts in southern Iraq.
- Editorial accuses U.N. Special Commission on Iraq of spying for Britain and the United States.
- More land reclaimed for cultivation in southern Iraq.
- Surge in textile production in Iraq.
